PullRequest.Title: sessions: hide footer action clicks from artifact activities
PullRequest.Body:

Clicking a general (footer) action in the artifact details view recorded a run that then showed up in the Activities list. These clicks are now omitted from Activities.

Runs of footer actions still appear when:
- they were triggered by automation,
- they were requested by an agent,
- their outcome is indeterminate, because the footer button directs the user to reconcile them in Activities.

The run is still recorded, so the footer button keeps showing its busy state. The same filter is used for history paging and for deciding whether the Activities card appears. The design proposal is updated to match.

### How to test

1. Open the details of an artifact whose integration contributes a general action.
2. Click that footer action.
3. Verify that no new entry appears in Activities.

### Validation

- `node_modules/.bin/tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck`: passed
- `node_modules/.bin/eslint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/artifactIntegrationPresentation.test.ts --browser chromium-msedge --grep Activities` (against a `tsc`-emitted `out/`, because pnpm and esbuild were unavailable locally): 21 passing, including the new test. The new test fails when the filter is removed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The constructor path, 50-run page size, awaited loop, and history protocol boundary are explicit. Only the prevalence of histories exceeding 50 footer clicks is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Artifact-history IPC calls, serialized run pages, and repeated history scans
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For H consecutive user footer runs, opening details performs ceil(H/50) serial getRuns calls; reopening repeats the scan. Composite models also rescan source-history prefixes for successive cursors.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive IPC and CPU work with increased activity-card resolution latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Footer runs were visible, so a collapsed open made no history request when one was in the snapshot; an expanded view stopped after its first fetched page.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: User footer-action runs now count as hidden, so loadPage serially fetches 50-run pages until another activity is found or history ends.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 140 now applies the snapshot-aware predicate; RIGHT lines 263-264 newly reject user general-action runs, so pages that previously ended the loop now trigger another getRuns call.
Findings.Title: Bound automatic paging through hidden footer runs
Findings.Impact: Opening an artifact with a long history of repeated general-action clicks can issue a serial cascade of history RPCs even while Activities is collapsed, increasing IPC/CPU work and delaying resolution of the card.
Findings.Evidence: Snapshots retain the latest 50 runs (artifactIntegrationService.ts:338). Opening details creates this model, and its autorun invokes loadPage when all snapshot runs are hidden (lines 84-89). The loop at lines 140-146 awaits getRuns(..., 50) for every all-hidden page. getRuns uses the ArtifactIntegrationProtocol history request, while CompositeArtifactModel.getRuns fans out to backing models and restarts from their newest pages on each outer request.
Findings.Recommendation: Bound automatic discovery and defer deeper scanning to explicit demand, or expose one filtered/seek history operation so finding the first displayable run does not require one client RPC per 50 hidden records.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open artifact details when the latest durable runs are user clicks on general/footer actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The panel mounts immediately, but the Activities card cannot settle its visibility/content until ArtifactActivitiesModel's automatic loadPage scan finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and serialize a 50-run artifact history page across the artifact integration protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After the diff, ceil(H/50) serial UI-level calls for H consecutive hidden user-footer runs, until a visible run or end of history; composite models may issue multiple backing-source page calls per UI request while seeking each cursor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A footer run was visible, so the 50-run snapshot prevented any collapsed-view history request. The new predicate makes that same snapshot/page hidden and enters the automatic scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not block mounting the whole details panel, but keeps Activities loading/unresolved and consumes host/client IPC and history-scan CPU.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H unique consecutive user-initiated general-action runs in durable history; no deduplication reduces this cardinality because every click has a distinct run ID.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Outer 50-run getRuns calls are strictly serial because each loop iteration awaits the previous call. CompositeArtifactModel may query its backing sources in parallel within one call, but there is no limiter or coalescing across repeated opens.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The newest 50 runs are already in the snapshot. Loaded pages are retained only by the current details model; closing and reopening creates a cold model and repeats the scan. CompositeArtifactModel restarts source merging from newest pages for each request rather than caching cursor state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: model construction, automatic trigger, page size, serial loop, and IPC implementation are all directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Histories exceeding 50 repeated footer clicks may be uncommon, but runs are durable and the call count is deterministic once that threshold is reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out introduced by treating a common durable run type as invisible in the existing auto-scan loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand Activities or request earlier history with mixed visible, automatic, agent, unreconciled, and footer runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One history page must return before rows and the Earlier Activities control update; additional pages are fetched only while a complete page is hidden.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch artifact run history in 50-row pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one call when the fetched page contains any visible run; grows by one per consecutive all-hidden 50-run page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Paging already existed and already skipped all-skipped pages; the diff materially increases all-hidden pages by adding ordinary user footer runs to that category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested Activities update waits for the page sequence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of consecutive all-hidden runs before the next visible run, after page grouping into batches of 50.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial page progression; one load is admitted at a time by the loading flag. Composite backing sources fan out in parallel per request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previously fetched pages are reused while the same details model is open. There is no cross-open cache or request coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call behavior and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mixed histories terminate quickly; the regression requires footer-only stretches spanning page boundaries.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the submitted fan-out finding; no separate duplicate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recompute and render the visible Activities list after snapshot updates or page loads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous derived-model work filters, deduplicates, sorts, and maps runs before updating the rendered/accessibility data.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to the 50 snapshot runs plus pages loaded in the current details lifetime, multiplied by contribution/general-action lookup cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded synchronous UI work; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary occurs during the predicate itself.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No visibility index is cached, but contribution and general-action collections are expected to be small; recomputation follows observable changes rather than frames or input events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the new predicate adds nested linear lookups; low evidence of user-visible cost at realistic cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider contribution/action counts are not formally capped here, but realistic counts are small and the added comparisons are cheap relative to existing sorting and item construction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the CPU work is not independently established as a concrete regression on a hot path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced details opening, history paging, rendering, protocol IPC, composite history merging, cache lifetime, and concurrency. Submitted one medium-confidence/high-mechanism-confidence boundary-fanout finding for serial automatic history scans through newly hidden footer runs.
